title: Finite-free complex fibre homology dimension is upper semicontinuous with quasi-compact sublevel sets
statement: Let $A$ be a ring and let $K$ be a bounded complex [def-pc-derived-category] of finite free $A$-modules, and fix an integer $i$. For each prime $\mathfrak p$ of $A$ put $b_i(\mathfrak p)=\dim_{\kappa(\mathfrak p)}H^i(K\otimes_A\kappa(\mathfrak p))$. Then $b_i$ is upper semicontinuous on $\operatorname{Spec}(A)$, and more precisely: for every integer $r$, the set $\{\mathfrak p:b_i(\mathfrak p)<r\}$ is a finite union of principal opens $D(f)$, $f\in A$; in particular it is open and quasi-compact.

proof.text: Choose finite bases of $K^{i-1},K^i,K^{i+1}$ by reindexing the finite chosen basis index sets to $\operatorname{Fin}(a),\operatorname{Fin}(c),\operatorname{Fin}(b)$. Let $M,N$ be the outgoing and incoming differential matrices. The private proved helper finiteFreeComplex_fibre_rank_formula transports the tensor-product bases through the scalar-extension equivalence and applies LinearMap.toMatrix_baseChange. Thus the residue-field matrices are $M(\mathfrak p),N(\mathfrak p)$ [def-weil-matrix-rank]. The source library's ShortComplex.finrank_homology_add_finrank_range_add_finrank_range applies rank-nullity [lem-weil-pbc-idempotent-charpoly-rank-nullity] to the outgoing map and the quotient of its kernel by the incoming image. Transport through homologyIsoSc' and rank_eq_finrank_range_toLin gives the additive identity $b_i(\mathfrak p)+\operatorname{rank}M(\mathfrak p)+\operatorname{rank}N(\mathfrak p)=c$. Only three terms are needed; the zero ring is handled since its prime spectrum is empty.

proof.text: For each natural number $s$, the private proved helper matrix_rank_locus applies the source library's Matrix.le_rank_map_iff to a finite matrix [def-weil-matrix-rank]. Its rank at a prime is at least $s$ exactly when some $s$ by $s$ minor has nonzero image in the residue field. Ideal.algebraMap_residueField_eq_zero identifies this with the prime not containing its determinant. The determinants of all pairs of functions from Fin s into the row and column index sets form a finite set, so the rank locus is a finite union of principal opens. This includes the size-zero determinant $1$; repeated rows or columns simply give zero determinants. The private proved helper principal_union_inter takes the finite image of products of two determinant families and uses $D(fg)=D(f)\cap D(g)$.

proof.text: The additive identity of Step 1 bounds both adjacent fibre ranks by $c$. For an integer threshold $r$, take the finite set of pairs $(x,y)\in\{0,\ldots,c\}^2$ satisfying $c<r+x+y$. The sublevel set $\{b_i<r\}$ equals the union, over these pairs, of the intersections of the rank loci $\{\operatorname{rank}M\ge x\}$ and $\{\operatorname{rank}N\ge y\}$. One inclusion uses the pair of actual ranks; the other uses the two lower rank bounds and the dimension identity. Lean's omega checks these natural-number and integer inequalities. Step 2 and the private proved helper principal_finite_union express this finite union as a finite union of principal opens. Each basic open is open and compact, and finite unions preserve both properties. Taking the nonnegative integer thresholds corresponding to natural-number thresholds proves upper semicontinuity. No new unfinished lemma is used.

lean.statement: theorem finiteFreeComplex_homology_upperSemicontinuous (A : Type u) [CommRing A] (K : CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{max u v} A) ℤ) (hbounded : ∃ a b : ℤ, K.IsStrictlyGE a ∧ K.IsStrictlyLE b) (hfree : ∀ n : ℤ, Module.Free A (K.X n) ∧ Module.Finite A (K.X n)) (i : ℤ) : ∃ β : PrimeSpectrum A → ℕ, (∀ p : PrimeSpectrum A, β p = Module.finrank p.asIdeal.ResidueField ((((ModuleCat.extendScalars.{u, u, max u v} (algebraMap A p.asIdeal.ResidueField)).mapHomologicalComplex (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).obj K).homology i)) ∧ UpperSemicontinuous β ∧ (∀ r : ℤ, ∃ s : Finset A, {p : PrimeSpectrum A | (β p : ℤ) < r} = ⋃ f ∈ (s : Set A), (PrimeSpectrum.basicOpen f : Set (PrimeSpectrum A))) ∧ (∀ r : ℤ, IsOpen {p : PrimeSpectrum A | (β p : ℤ) < r} ∧ IsCompact {p : PrimeSpectrum A | (β p : ℤ) < r})
